data.exact_reserve_text: The syndicate also benefitted from prior year releases of $4.3m (2014: $4.1m), which was a reflection of the continued low level of insured natural catastrophe losses incurred in the past 2 years.

named_events.event_name: explosions in the Chinese port of Tianjin
named_events.loss_description: The syndicate's largest loss to date on the 2015 underwriting year relates to the explosions in the Chinese port of Tianjin. However this loss is well within our catastrophe margin.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 6107 recorded an opening (prior-year) gross claims outstanding of 25.1122 million (USD). Management reports prior year releases of $4.3m (USD) which they attribute to continued low insured natural catastrophe activity and favourable claims development, resulting in an overall prior-year release (favourable) of approximately $4.3m. No explicit gross prior-year movement figure was provided, so the reported $4.3m is a net release figure disclosed by management.
raw_causal_phrases: prior year releases of $4.3m (2014: $4.1m), which was a reflection of the continued low level of insured natural catastrophe losses incurred in the past 2 years.
lower than average level of claims notifications
data.data_quality_notes: No explicit GROSS prior-year movement (insurance liabilities) is presented in the notes. The report explicitly states a prior year release of $4.3m but this is described in narrative as a net release (after reinsurance). The gross 'movement in provision' shown in the technical provisions relates to total movement (including current year) and cannot be used per the rules. A gross claims development triangle in the technical provisions is present but does not provide prior-period diagonals clearly enough to compute a gross PYD. Therefore the reported prior_year_development_gbp_m uses the management-disclosed net prior year release ($4.3m) as a last-resort fallback. Users should treat the prior-year movement as NET of reinsurance and of lower confidence for gross-reserve analysis.
